title: Samsung HBM4 Price Hike: Proposed 3x Increase for 2026
content:
Korea Supply Chain Brief · October 2, 2026

Samsung Electronics is reportedly pricing its next-generation HBM4 memory at more than three times the price of its current HBM3E chips for 2026 supply contracts, betting its performance lead justifies a steep premium. Here's what's been disclosed about the pricing talks and what it would mean for Samsung's memory business.

CompanyRoleEvidence
Samsung Electronics
KRX: 005930		Setting 2026 HBM4 annual supply pricing with major customersReported: exclusive report citing semiconductor industry sources, Oct 2, 2026

What's been disclosed

  • Price proposed: Samsung has proposed pricing in the mid-to-high $4-per-gigabit range for 2026 HBM4 supply, in ongoing annual contract negotiations with major customers.
  • More than 3x current pricing: That compares with roughly $1.50 per gigabit for Samsung's current flagship HBM3E, meaning the proposed HBM4 price is more than triple.
  • Annual contract structure: Unlike standard DRAM, HBM is overwhelmingly sold through annual long-term contracts in which customers and suppliers agree on next year's volume and price in advance — buyers lock in supply, and manufacturers plan production around it.
  • Timeline: Most of next year's HBM volume has reportedly already been agreed with customers, and price negotiations are expected to wrap up this month (October 2026).
  • Why it matters for Samsung's numbers: The price landing in these talks will directly set Samsung's 2026 HBM average selling price (ASP) and, by extension, the profitability of its memory business for the year.

Why this matters

HBM4 marks a generational transition for high-bandwidth memory used in AI accelerators, and Samsung is reportedly using the changeover to push pricing power rather than compete mainly on cost. A successful premium at this scale would be a significant profitability lever for Samsung's memory division heading into 2026, given how large a share of AI hardware cost now sits in HBM. (Reported)

What's still unconfirmed

No customer names were disclosed, and the final negotiated price has not been confirmed — the $4-mid-to-high figure is Samsung's proposed starting point, not necessarily the settled rate. Volume commitments tied to this pricing round, and how competitors' HBM4 pricing compares, were also not disclosed. (Reported)

Quick FAQ

Is this the final price customers will pay?
Not confirmed. This is the price Samsung has proposed in negotiations; the settled price could differ once talks conclude, reportedly later this month.

Why would customers accept 3x the price?
Based on current reporting, Samsung is pricing on HBM4's performance lead rather than cost, and because most 2026 volume has already been agreed, customers locking in supply have limited leverage to push back hard on price.

Does this affect Samsung's overall earnings outlook?
The article frames this price as the key variable that will set Samsung's 2026 HBM average selling price and memory division profitability, though exact earnings impact was not quantified.

Source (Korean): Maeil Business Newspaper (매일경제), Oct 2, 2026, reporter Park So-ra. https://www.mk.co.kr/news/business/12167164
